Drummer David “Panama” Francis has been performing professionally since the 1930’s. A native of Miami, David played his first engagements with the Florida Collegians and in New York with Tab Smith. Later gigs with Billy Hicks, Roy Eldridge, Lucky Millinder and Cab Calloway made him a familiar and sought-after drummer for both recordings and live shows. The studios in New York City have called on Panama frequently since the 1950’s and he has played on hundreds of Jazz, Rhythm & Blues and early Rock records. In later years he has led the Savoy Sultans and been honored by the Rhythm & Blues Foundation. He is a founding member of the Statesmen of Jazz and can be seen at jazz festivals across the country.
